To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the response to the muons is uniform over the whole detector area, the response is linear with energy, the response is stable with time, and the energy resolution is better than 50% for the energy range from 1 to 20 GeV.
the response to muons in the stack of nine RPC layers is linear, and that the energy resolution for muons is 30%/$\sqrt{E}$.

the digital hadron calorimenter is capable of measuring hadronic showers with a resolution of 0.3 in units of the mean shower energy and that the calorimeter is able to measure the energy of muons with a resolution of about 2%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of digital hadron calorimeters for the LHC and the calibration and performance evaluation of a prototype of such a calorimeter.
the development and application of new methods of data analysis for high energy physics, in particular, for the search for new phenomena in the data collected by the ATLAS experiment at the LHC.
the study of the properties of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) produced in relativistic nuclear collisions.

the digital hadron calorimetry is feasible and that the digital calorimeter can be calibrated using muons.
the digital hadron calorimetry technique has been proven to be a viable alternative to analog calorimetry.

the digital hadron calorimetry is feasible and that the energy resolution of a digital hadronic calorimeter with Resistice Plate Chambers can be comparable with that of the analog calorimeters.
we have demonstrated that the digital hadron calorimeters can provide a high level of performance for particle identification.
